subject: Post-demo alignment — hosted pilot scope, sandbox endpoints & rate ceilings
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Desai <amit@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo alignment — hosted pilot scope, sandbox endpoints & rate ceilings

Hi Amit,

Great demo today — thanks for walking through your prompt flows and sample transcripts. Recap + suggested next steps below so we can align on a lightweight hosted pilot.

Summary from our call:
- Goal: validate inference quality and latency for customer support triage + short-form summarization (avg 120 tokens in, 40 tokens out).
- Target peak concurrency: ~40 RPS during business hours; sustained 8–12 RPS outside peak.
- Data controls: non-PII only for this pilot; Finlytics will provide scrubbed transcripts.

Suggested hosted quickstart plan (what we can provision in week 1):
1) Sandbox endpoints: 2 endpoints — "triage-v1" (short latency SLO) and "summarize-v1" (higher context).
2) Rate ceilings: set initial per-endpoint token caps at 80k tokens/min for triage and 20k tokens/min for summarize. We can tighten/loosen after observing real traffic.
3) Auth: single sandbox API key for your engineering team (rotateable).
4) Observability: we'll add token-level cost and latency dashboards scoped to your endpoints.
5) Success criteria: avg 95th-pct latency < 400ms for triage endpoint and acceptable quality for summarization on 50 eval prompts.

Attachments: I attached a short pilot-scope PDF with the above and a provisioning checklist (pilot-scope.pdf).

Questions / asks for you:
- Can you confirm the 40 RPS peak estimate and give a ballpark for average tokens per request across both flows?
- Any regulatory constraints on keeping logs in US-only regions for this pilot?
- Who on your side should I add to the sandbox access list?

Next steps (proposed):
- You confirm traffic numbers and access list by EOD Tue.
- I’ll have Ops stand up the sandbox endpoints and provide keys within 48 hours of your confirmation.

Looping in Monica to provision once we have your thumbs-up.

Thanks —
Rishi
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rm@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0173

From: Amit Desai <amit@finlytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-13T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo alignment — hosted pilot scope, sandbox endpoints & rate ceilings

Thanks Rishi — helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic: 40 RPS peak sounds right for an initial pilot. Average tokens per request is roughly 140 (prompt+context) in and 45 out for triage; summaries are heavier — ~600 in / ~80 out on sample set.
- Data residency: for now we need logs and audit traces to stay in US regions due to our compliance posture.
- Access list: please add myself (amit@finlytics.com), Priya Rao (priya.rao@finlytics.com) and our infra lead Rahul Mehta (rahul.mehta@finlytics.com).

Two other asks: 
1) Can you confirm how rate limiting behaves at the API key vs endpoint level? We want to ensure a single key doesn’t get throttled in a way that prevents parallel use across endpoints.
2) For the summarization flow we may want to test a cached prefix path for repeated contexts — can your sandbox enable prefix/KV cache emulation?

If hosted evaluation looks good we’ll loop in procurement for terms; otherwise we may need to discuss dedicated capacity, but we prefer to validate hosted first.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Amit
Head of Integrations, Finlytics
amit@finlytics.com | +1 646-555-0124

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Desai <amit@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-13T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo alignment — hosted pilot scope, sandbox endpoints & rate ceilings

Thanks Amit — great detail, that helps a lot. Answers inline below and updated plan.

- Rate limiting behavior: Redwood supports both API-key-level and endpoint-level limits. For the sandbox we’ll provision per-endpoint ceilings (so one noisy endpoint won’t throttle the other). We’ll also set a bucketed API-key burst allowance to avoid token delays when you switch flows.

- KV/prefix cache emulation: yes — we can enable an emulation layer in sandbox so your team can validate hit rates. It won’t be identical to production caching performance but will be suitable for functional validation.

Updated rate ceilings (proposed):
- triage-v1: 90k tokens/min, 60 concurrent requests (soft limit)
- summarize-v1: 30k tokens/min, 12 concurrent requests (soft limit)
- API key burst: 100 concurrent token-burst allowance across endpoints for short spikes.

Security & residency: we’ll ensure logs/audit traces for your sandbox are pinned to our US region and won’t be replicated to other regions for the duration of the pilot. Monica — can you enable a US-only retention policy for the Finlytics sandbox?

Sandbox provisioning plan: once you confirm the access list and agree on the ceilings, Monica will provide endpoint URLs and temporary API keys. I’ve added a Drive provisioning checklist link in the attachments (sandbox-provisioning-instructions.md) and included a HubSpot deal link in the thread metadata.

If you’re happy, I’ll mark the pilot kickoff for Thursday and Monica will aim to deliver keys within 48 hours.

Regards,
Rishi

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>; Amit Desai <amit@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo alignment — hosted pilot scope, sandbox endpoints & rate ceilings

Hi Amit / Rishi —

Provisioning update: I’ve stood up the requested sandbox endpoints in the US region. Details below (temporary credentials attached in the Drive link):

- Endpoint: https://sandbox.us.redwood.ai/finlytics/triage-v1
  - API key: SK-sbx-fin-TRG-xxxx (rotate after first use)
  - Initial ceilings: 90k tokens/min, soft concurrency 60

- Endpoint: https://sandbox.us.redwood.ai/finlytics/summarize-v1
  - API key: SK-sbx-fin-SUM-xxxx
  - Initial ceilings: 30k tokens/min, soft concurrency 12

- Cache emulation: Enabled (kv-prefix-mode on). Hit-rate logs will be available in the sandbox observability view.
- Log residency: All audit logs retained in US-only storage bucket for this pilot (90-day retention).

Attachments: sandbox provisioning doc in Drive with quick test curl commands and sample prompts (see related link).

If you see any throttling during your tests, flag the exact request ids and timestamps and we’ll adjust ceilings quickly. I’ll also schedule a 30-min ops sync Friday to walk through metrics and adjust runbook thresholds.

Thanks — Monica
Platform Ops, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
